Introduction
Diindolylmethanes (DIMs) are one class of unique and privi-
leged indole alkaloids among numerous natural products,
exhibiting a wide range of biological activities, 1 such as anti-
inflammatory,1a,b antiproliferative,1c antihyperlipidemic,1d
anti-cancer1e and GPR84 agonistic activity. 1f Moreover, DIMs
are also recognized as core building blocks in the research of
colorimetric chemosensors to prepare conjugated tris(indolyl)
methane anion receptors

plify. Oxidative addition of allenamide 1a to the active Pd(0)
catalyst generates the Pd( II) species I, which undergoes an
intramolecular Heck reaction to achieve the π-allylpalladium
species II.16 The triple bond of o-ethynylaniline 2a coordinates
to intermediate II to produce intermediate III by ligand
exchange. In the presence of base, species III could easily
convert to species IV.17 Finally, the C –C reductive elimination
of species IV produces diindolylmethane 3aa and regenerates
the Pd(0) species to the next catalyzed cycle.
